name: Auroville
note: Universal township near Puducherry inaugurated 1968 with UNESCO backing; ~3,300 residents from ~60 nations; own schools, farms and reforested plateau.

name: Sadhana Forest
note: Volunteer-run reforestation and water-harvesting community beside Auroville; sister projects in Haiti and Kenya.

name: Navdanya Farm / Bija Vidyapeeth
note: Vandana Shiva's organic seed-bank farm and 'Earth University' in the Doon Valley near Dehradun.

name: Mitraniketan
note: Rural education and development community founded 1956 at Vellanad near Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala.

name: Timbaktu Collective
note: Regenerated degraded drylands in Anantapur district; runs farmer cooperatives, forest commons and an alternative school.

name: Govardhan Ecovillage
note: Krishna-devotee ecovillage in Palghar district; organic farming, natural building and sustainability training centre.

name: Sarvodaya Shramadana (HQ)
note: Gandhian-Buddhist village development movement since 1958, active in ~15,000 Sri Lankan villages; HQ at Moratuwa.

name: Himalayan Permaculture Centre
note: Surkhet-based network training mid-hill farming communities in permaculture across western Nepal.

name: Findhorn Ecovillage
note: Founded 1962 near Findhorn, Moray; hosted the 1995 conference that launched GEN; whisky-barrel houses, wind turbines, Living Machine.

name: Lammas (Tir y Gafel)
note: Nine off-grid smallholdings near Glandwr, Pembrokeshire; pioneer of Welsh low-impact (One Planet) planning.

name: Brithdir Mawr
note: Pembrokeshire community famous for Tony Wrench's turf-roofed roundhouse planning battle.

name: Cloughjordan Ecovillage
note: Ireland's flagship ecovillage on 67 acres in Co. Tipperary; district heating, community farm, eco-enterprise centre.

name: Tamera
note: Peace-research village near Odemira (Alentejo); water-retention landscape and solar test field; ~170 residents.

name: Mosaic Village
note: Young regenerative ecovillage in the Alentejo, part of Portugal's fast-growing community scene.

name: Matavenero
note: Abandoned El Bierzo (León) village resettled from 1989 by Rainbow-movement founders; no road access, off-grid.

name: Lakabe
note: Abandoned Navarre village occupied in 1980 and later legalised; communal bakery, own energy; anchor of Iberian network.

name: Los Portales
note: Long-running community near Castilblanco de los Arroyos, Seville; organic farm and education.

name: Arterra Bizimodu
note: Ecovillage in Artieda, Navarre (Pre-Pyrenees); international volunteers and GEN Europe activities.

name: Sunseed Desert Technology
note: Volunteer community testing solar cooking and dryland techniques in Los Molinos del Río Aguas, Almería, since 1986.

name: Damanhur
note: Federation of communities in Valchiusella (Piedmont) with own constitution and currency; famous underground Temples of Humankind.

name: Torri Superiore
note: Medieval hamlet near Ventimiglia restored by a cultural association since 1989; guesthouse and permaculture courses.

name: Popolo Elfico
note: 'Elves' of the Valle dei Burroni (Tuscan-Emilian Apennines): hamlets re-inhabited without grid power since the early 1980s.

name: Sieben Linden
note: Straw-bale and timber ecovillage in the Altmark; ~140 residents; studied for its very low per-capita carbon footprint.

name: ZEGG
note: Centre for Experimental Culture Design in Bad Belzig; origin of the 'Forum' communication method.

name: Lebensgarten Steyerberg
note: Converted 1930s settlement in Lower Saxony turned into an ecological and spiritual community.

name: Schloss Tempelhof
note: Castle estate in Kreßberg (Baden-Württemberg) since 2010; ~150 people, own free school and solidarity farming.

name: Kommune Niederkaufungen
note: One of Germany's largest income-sharing communes near Kassel; consensus decisions and collective businesses.

name: Vauban (Freiburg)
note: Car-reduced eco-district on a former barracks; resident-led planning (Forum Vauban) and passive/plus-energy houses.

name: Schweibenalp
note: Alpine 'Center of Unity' above Lake Brienz; seminar centre and permaculture gardens.

name: Schloss Glarisegg
note: Lakeside manor on Untersee (Thurgau) run by a residential community since 2003.

name: Ecodorp Boekel
note: 36 social-rental eco-homes in North Brabant (residents from 2016); the Netherlands' flagship ecovillage.

name: EVA-Lanxmeer
note: Ecological neighbourhood of ~240 homes in Culemborg built 1994-2009 with water-protection permaculture design.

name: Christiania
note: Squatted Copenhagen barracks since 1971; residents bought the land collectively in 2012.

name: Svanholm
note: Manor estate bought by 100+ people in 1978; organic farming collective west of Copenhagen.

name: Dyssekilde
note: Ecovillage at Torup near Hundested with self-built ecological houses.

name: Munksøgård
note: Five cohousing groups near Roskilde with mixed tenure; early adopter of urine-separating toilets.

name: Hurdal Ecovillage
note: Norway's largest ecovillage, 70 km north of Oslo; low-energy timber homes and a community farm.

name: Sólheimar
note: Founded 1930 by Sesselja Sigmundsdóttir; inclusive community with disabled residents, organic farming, geothermal heat.

name: Ängsbacka
note: Personal-development course and festival centre in Molkom, Värmland, with a resident community.

name: Suderbyn
note: Permaculture eco-village near Visby, Gotland; research on closed-loop greenhouses.

name: Understenshöjden
note: Resident-built ecological housing association in Björkhagen, Stockholm, adjoining the Nacka nature reserve.

name: Keuruu Ecovillage
note: Rural ecovillage in Central Finland, one of the country's few established intentional communities.

name: Plum Village
note: Founded 1982 by Thich Nhat Hanh in the Dordogne; Europe's largest Buddhist monastery.

name: Taizé Community
note: Ecumenical brotherhood of ~100 brothers in Burgundy receiving tens of thousands of young visitors a year.

name: Longo Maï (Limans)
note: Anti-capitalist farming co-operative network founded 1973 at Limans, Provence, now spread across Europe and Costa Rica.

name: Krishna Valley
note: Self-sufficient Hare Krishna valley near Somogyvámos; organic farming and ox power.

name: Gyűrűfű
note: Abandoned Baranya hamlet revived as an ecovillage from 1991 near Ibafa.

name: Kovcheg (Ark)
note: Kaluga-region settlement of 1-ha family homesteads; among the best known of Russia's Anastasia 'kin domain' villages.

name: Lilleoru
note: Spiritual practice and eco-building community in Kuusalu parish, east of Tallinn.

name: Green Commune Belica
note: Mountain-village commune in western North Macedonia (Kičevo area).

name: Kalikalos
note: Summer holistic-education community on Mt Pelion run since 2001.

name: Dedetepe
note: Eco-farm near the Kaz Dağları (Çanakkale) hosting volunteers and permaculture courses.

name: Kibbutz Lotan
note: Reform-Jewish kibbutz in the Arava desert; Center for Creative Ecology teaches mud building and permaculture.

name: Degania Alef
note: World's first kibbutz (1910) by the Sea of Galilee - precedent for ~270 kibbutzim.

name: Neve Shalom / Wahat al-Salam
note: Cooperative village of Jewish and Palestinian-Arab citizens with a bilingual school and School for Peace.

name: Kibbutz Ketura
note: Arava kibbutz hosting the Arava Institute for Environmental Studies and an early commercial solar field.

name: Zanasouj Ecovillage
note: Mountain ecovillage project in Qazvin province.

name: Sekem
note: Ibrahim Abouleish's 1977 biodynamic desert-reclamation community near Belbeis; schools, clinic and Heliopolis University.

name: Kufunda Village
note: Learning village on the outskirts of Harare teaching permaculture and community leadership.

name: Guédé Chantier
note: Large Senegal River village (Podor) and model site in Senegal's national ecovillage programme.

name: Lynedoch EcoVillage
note: Mixed-income ecovillage and Sustainability Institute near Stellenbosch.

name: Kuthumba
note: Rural ecovillage on the Garden Route near Plettenberg Bay.

name: Ndanifor Permaculture Eco-Village
note: Permaculture and youth-training hub near Bafut/Bamenda in north-west Cameroon.

name: SINA - Social Innovation Academy
note: Self-organised learning community for marginalised youth near Mpigi; model replicated in several African countries.

name: Sadhana Forest Kenya
note: Sadhana Forest's Samburu project planting food forests with pastoralist communities.

name: Konohana Family
note: Natural-farming 'one big family' of ~100 people with a shared economy at the foot of Mt Fuji (Fujinomiya).

name: Atarashiki-mura
note: 'New Village' utopian commune founded 1918 by Mushanokōji Saneatsu; moved to Moroyama, Saitama, in 1939.

name: Seonae Ville
note: Rural intentional community in North Chungcheong listed on the GEN map (self-reported ~150 people).

name: Hua Dao Ecovillage
note: Ecovillage and education project on the Chengdu plain, Sichuan.

name: Pun Pun
note: Organic farm and seed centre near Chiang Mai co-founded by Jon Jandai; popularised mud-house building in Thailand.

name: Wongsanit Ashram
note: Engaged-Buddhist community and training centre in Nakhon Nayok linked to Sulak Sivaraksa's network.

name: Maia Earth Village
note: Ecovillage project in Palawan.

name: Umai Ecovillage
note: Self-described first ecovillage in Kazakhstan, near Almaty.

name: Crystal Waters
note: World's first designed permaculture village (Conondale, Qld); 1996 World Habitat Award; 85-lot body corporate.

name: Narara Ecovillage
note: Co-operative ecovillage on a former horticultural research station near Gosford, NSW; shared microgrid.

name: The Ecovillage at Currumbin
note: Off-mains-water eco-subdivision in the Gold Coast hinterland.

name: Moora Moora
note: Co-operative of six hamlets on 245 ha near Healesville, Victoria, founded 1974.

name: Tuntable Falls Co-operative
note: Born from the 1973 Aquarius Festival at Nimbin; archetype of NSW multiple-occupancy communities.

name: Tui Community
note: Long-running community at Wainui Bay, Golden Bay, with organic gardens and workshops.

name: Otamatea Eco-Village
note: Rural ecovillage on the Kaipara Harbour, Northland, with native forest restoration.

name: Earthsong Eco-Neighbourhood
note: Rammed-earth cohousing neighbourhood in Ranui, West Auckland.

name: Edenhope Nature Preserve
note: Small permaculture/nature-preserve community on Espiritu Santo.

name: The Farm
note: Founded 1971 by Stephen Gaskin's caravan in Summertown, Tennessee; pioneered midwifery, soy foods and Plenty International.

name: Twin Oaks
note: Walden Two-inspired income-sharing commune in Louisa, Virginia; hammock and tofu businesses.

name: East Wind Community
note: Ozarks income-sharing commune known for its nut-butter business.

name: Dancing Rabbit Ecovillage
note: 280-acre ecovillage near Rutledge, Missouri, with strict ecological covenants (no private cars).

name: Earthaven Ecovillage
note: Off-grid permaculture ecovillage on 329 forested acres near Black Mountain, North Carolina.

name: EcoVillage at Ithaca
note: Three cohousing neighbourhoods (FROG, SONG, TREE) with organic farms on West Hill, Ithaca.

name: Arcosanti
note: Paolo Soleri's experimental 'arcology' town in the Arizona desert, under construction since 1970.

name: Sirius Community
note: Findhorn-inspired spiritual community in Shutesbury, Massachusetts, founded by former Findhorn members.

name: Breitenbush
note: Worker-owned hot-springs retreat community in the Oregon Cascades with off-grid hydro and geothermal heat.

name: Los Angeles Eco-Village
note: Two-block urban retrofit in Koreatown, LA, since 1993; car-light living and community land trust.

name: Lama Foundation
note: Mountain spiritual community north of Taos, New Mexico, founded 1967; Ram Dass's 'Be Here Now' was produced here.

name: Koinonia Farm
note: Interracial Christian farming community in Sumter County, Georgia (1942); birthplace of Habitat for Humanity.

name: Cité Écologique
note: Quebec ecovillage at Ham-Nord with its own school, organic farm and businesses.

name: O.U.R. Ecovillage
note: Permaculture demonstration ecovillage at Shawnigan Lake, Vancouver Island; natural-building education.

name: Yarrow Ecovillage
note: Mixed-use ecovillage with cohousing and organic farm in Yarrow, Chilliwack, BC.

name: Whole Village
note: Rural ecovillage and farm near Caledon, Ontario.

name: Huehuecoyotl
note: Artists' ecovillage in the hills of Tepoztlán, Morelos, settled 1982 by a travelling theatre troupe.

name: Las Cañadas
note: Cloud-forest restoration and agroecology cooperative near Huatusco, Veracruz.

name: Los Horcones
note: Behaviour-analysis-based community near Hermosillo, Sonora, inspired by Skinner's Walden Two.

name: Pachamama
note: Meditation-centred eco-community near Nosara on the Nicoya Peninsula.

name: Rancho Mastatal
note: Rainforest farm-community in Puriscal teaching natural building and permaculture.

name: Maya Mountain Research Farm
note: Permaculture/agroforestry farm restoring degraded land in Toledo District since 1988.

name: Finca El Zopilote
note: Permaculture farm-community on Ometepe Island, Lake Nicaragua.

name: Ecovilla Gaia
note: Asociacion Gaia's pioneering ecovillage and GEN education centre in Navarro, Buenos Aires province.

name: Comunidad Ecológica de Peñalolén
note: Low-density eco-community in Santiago's Andean foothills with strong environmental covenants.

name: Atlántida
note: Mountain ecovillage near Cajibío, Cauca; location per OpenStreetMap.

name: Aldeafeliz
note: Ecovillage in San Francisco, Cundinamarca, north-west of Bogotá.

name: Nashira
note: Ecovillage of low-income, female-headed families near Palmira, Valle del Cauca.

name: Gaviotas
note: Paolo Lugari's 1971 experimental village in the Llanos (Vichada); reforested large areas of savanna.

name: Piracanga
note: Spiritual ecovillage on Bahia's Maraú peninsula between rainforest and beach.

name: Céu do Mapiá
note: Santo Daime religious village deep in the Amazonas rainforest, founded 1983.

name: Arca Verde
note: Ecovillage in São Francisco de Paula, Rio Grande do Sul.

name: Ecoaldea Paititi
note: Ecovillage project in Bolivia's northern lowlands (La Paz dept.).

name: Eco Truly Park
note: Hare Krishna ecovillage with adobe 'trulli' domes on the desert coast near Chancay.

name: Ecoaldea Tierra Madre
note: Young ecovillage in Lavalleja department, Uruguay.

name: Aldeas de Paz
note: Small community in the Gran Sabana (Bolívar state).
